# `get_sequence`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Return one sequence entry by position in the map.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (full command-socket call; shared diagnostic writes; 64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xc1a20 (64-bit build) |

Looks the entry up by zero-based position, not by id. Negative or out-of-range indices give 209. The grade reflects the whole request/reply path, which reaches the shared diagnostic logger; it does not by itself mean the method changes device settings.

Side effects: Copies one entry under the sequence mutex. Every call also performs shared request/reply diagnostic logging.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_sequence"`. [READ] |
| `params` | integer\|array | yes | - | Required zero-based index into the sequence map in map order (not an entry id): an integer, or a positional array whose first element is used. Absent, null, empty array, object, or a non-integer (including float) gives 104. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (get_sequence reply (success)) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | object | yes | - | (get_sequence reply (success)) Entry at that index. All twelve members are always emitted. [READ] |
| `result.id` | integer | yes | - | (get_sequence reply (success)) Entry id. [READ] |
| `result.type` | string | yes | - | (get_sequence reply (success)) Frame type name. One of: `light`, `dark`, `bias`, `flat`, `unknown`. [READ] |
| `result.filter` | integer | yes | - | (get_sequence reply (success)) Filter slot index. [READ] |
| `result.suffix` | string | yes | - | (get_sequence reply (success)) File name suffix. [READ] |
| `result.exp` | number | yes | - | (get_sequence reply (success)) Exposure; unit not established. [READ] |
| `result.gain` | integer | yes | - | (get_sequence reply (success)) Gain; scale not established. [READ] |
| `result.bin` | integer | yes | - | (get_sequence reply (success)) Binning factor (INFERRED). [INFERRED] |
| `result.repeat` | integer | yes | - | (get_sequence reply (success)) Frames to capture (INFERRED count). [INFERRED] |
| `result.lapsed` | integer | yes | - | (get_sequence reply (success)) Frames captured so far (INFERRED count); the progress that reset_sequence_progress clears. [INFERRED] |
| `result.capture_index` | integer | yes | - | (get_sequence reply (success)) Capture-control selector (INFERRED); meaning not established. [INFERRED] |
| `result.enable` | boolean | yes | - | (get_sequence reply (success)) Entry is active. [READ] |
| `result.autoexp` | boolean | yes | - | (get_sequence reply (success)) Auto exposure flag. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (get_sequence reply (success)) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (get_sequence reply (success)) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 104 | params is not an integer or an array whose first element is an integer | `expected int param` |
| 209 | No entry at that index (empty map, past the end, or negative) | `invalid value` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

## Example

Request, first - Entry at index 0:

```json
{"id":81,"method":"get_sequence","params":[0]}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_sequence","result":{"id":1,"type":"light","filter":0,"suffix":"L","exp":10,"gain":80,"bin":1,"repeat":30,"lapsed":5,"capture_index":0,"enable":true,"autoexp":false},"code":0,"id":81}
```

Reply, no-such-index:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_sequence","error":"invalid value","code":209,"id":82}
```
